## What the evidence is — and what it is not

This is the **IG-ONLY ablation**: I have mean |IG| magnitudes per feature, averaged over all cells, with **no sign (direction), no per-cell values, no subgroup statistics, and no decision rules**. That constrains what any hypothesis from this list can claim.

Two structural facts about the data are visible in the ranking itself:

1. **The feature space is a mixed-species transcriptome.** A coherent block of *mouse* housekeeping genes carries attribution comparable to top human markers: MOUSE_Neat1 (#15), Gnb2 (#23), Rpl8 (#26), Cald1 (#29), H3f3b (#33), Cox4i1 (#38), Cited2 (#41), Lmna (#43), Actb (#46), the Cox6a/b/c cluster (#59–63), B2m (#69), Calm1/2 (#78/81), Malat1 (#100). Mouse genes can only receive non-zero IG if they are actually expressed in a cell subpopulation — so the dataset contains mouse cells, and "being a mouse cell" is one of the strongest predictors of the CD45RA antibody signal (expected near background, since anti-human CD45RA does not bind mouse Ptpc; species-mixing designs of exactly this kind, with mouse cells as antibody-staining negative controls, appear in published CITE-seq datasets such as Stoeckius et al., Nat Methods 2017).

2. **The top human features decompose into canonical lineage blocks**, not into a single regulatory module:
   - **Cytotoxic NK/CD8 program:** GNLY (#1), NKG7 (#2), GZMA (#3), GZMB (#6), CMC1 (#9), CD8B (#10), CLIC3 (#11), KLRB1 (#17), KLRF1 (#18), CTSW (#22), STAT4 (#25), TRDC (#28), CST7 (#30), KLRD1 (#31), CCL5 (#32), IL2RB (#40), CD8A (#44), CD160, FGFBP2, PRF1, GZMH, GZMK, XCL1/2, KLRC1, NCR3, RUNX3, TBX21, IFNG.
   - **Monocyte/myeloid program:** CST3 (#4), S100A12 (#5), FCN1 (#8), LGALS2 (#12), S100B (#13), LGALS1 (#14), MNDA (#16), LYZ (#19), HLA-DRB1 (#20), CD14 (#21), IFI30 (#24), CLEC4E, IRF8, MAFB, IRF7, HLA-DRA/DPA1/DQA1, MS4A7, S100A8/A9, VCAN, ITGAM, TREM1, PLD4, LILRA4 (pDC).
   - **B-cell program:** IGHV1OR15-1 (#27), TCL1A (#42), IGHM (#45), CD79A (#58), CD79B, IGHD, MS4A1, IGJ, VPREB3, IGLL1, FCRL1/3, EBF1, MZB1.
   - **Erythroid program:** HBG1 (#87), GATA1, GYPB, HBA1/HBA2, HBG2, ALAS2, AHSP, HBM, HBE1, HBZ.
   - **Megakaryocyte/platelet program:** PPBP (#207), GP9, SDPR, RGS18, PF4, TUBB1.
   - Plus one uncharacterized lncRNA (RP11-1143G9.4, #7) whose identity I cannot resolve from this evidence.

3. **Equally informative is what is absent:** **PTPRC itself** (the gene encoding CD45) is not among the 1500 features; nor are the canonical pan-T/naive-T markers (CD3D/E, CD4, IL7R, CCR7, LEF1, TCF7, SELL, CD27, CD28, TRAC/TRBC). No known PTPRC-splicing regulatory factors (SRSF/hnRNP-class) appear either.

## Narrative

CD45RA is not a plain gene-expression level: it is an antibody epitope whose signal depends on (i) how much PTPRC a cell produces, (ii) whether variable exon 4 (the "A" exon) is included, and (iii) species-specific antibody binding. Gene-level RNA cannot encode (ii) directly — it can only predict it *through cell state*. The IG profile is precisely the signature of a model that has done so: attribution mass sits on lineage- and differentiation-state-defining genes, i.e., on the axes along which CD45RA protein abundance actually varies across a mixed mononuclear-cell sample. The CD45RA-high population (naive T cells) is represented only obliquely (CD8A/B) or by exclusion, because its own marker program was not available to the model. This also means the ranking describes CD45RA prediction across the full mixture, not regulation within the nominal CD45RA+ naive T-cell population.

## Single best hypothesis

**CD45RA surface abundance in this dataset is regulated primarily at the level of cell lineage and lymphocyte differentiation state — i.e., by which PTPRC isoform program each cell carries — rather than by any single upstream transcriptomic regulator acting within naive T cells.** The dominant lymphoid axis runs between the naive T-cell state (CD45RA-high) and the cytotoxic NK/CD8 effector state (expected CD45RA-low / CD45RO-positive, per the activation-induced RA→RO isoform switch), while the monocyte, B, erythroid, megakaryocytic, and mouse-cell blocks define the middle and floor of the CD45RA distribution (mouse, erythroid, and platelet-signature cells should sit at antibody background).

**Testable predictions:** (1) signed per-cell IG or direct regression should show *negative* association of GNLY/NKG7/GZMA/GZMB/CMC1/CLIC3 with CD45RA among CD3+ lymphocytes and positive attribution for CD8B among CD8 T cells; (2) CD45RA ADT should be at/near background in mouse-gene-high, HBG/HBA-high, and PPBP/PF4-high cells; (3) re-fitting within sorted naive T cells should collapse the attribution of all these lineage markers — residual top features in that setting would be the real candidates for within-naive-T CD45RA regulation (none can be nominated from the present evidence); (4) adding PTPRC, CD3D/E, CD4, IL7R, CCR7, LEF1, TCF7, SELL to the feature set should make them dominate the ranking; (5) exon-4 junction-level PTPRC quantification should out-predict any gene-level feature within the T-cell compartment.

## Established knowledge vs. new mechanism

This is primarily **(a) confirmation of established literature**: CD45RA is the high-molecular-weight PTPRC isoform of resting/naive lymphocytes, and activation/differentiation is accompanied by loss of CD45RA and gain of CD45RO (Akbar et al., Nature 1988; isoform structure from alternative splicing of PTPRC exons 4–6: Streuli et al., J Exp Med 1988; Trowbridge & Thomas, Annu Rev Immunol 1994; regulation of this splicing by RNA-binding/splicing factors has been characterized by K. W. Lynch and colleagues). The modest **(b)** element is the dataset-level claim that RNA→CD45RA prediction here is almost entirely cell-identity inference, with the cytotoxic program carrying the single largest block of attribution — directly testable as above.

## Honest limits of this IG-only evidence

From this ranking alone I **cannot** determine: the sign of any feature's effect; whether NK cells in this sample are CD45RA-high or -low; whether any within-naive-T gradient of CD45RA exists; or any splicing/transcription-factor mechanism (the relevant features are absent from the list). To reach a mechanistic hypothesis I would need: signed per-cell IG attributions; per-cluster CD45RA ADT distributions; the subgroup/conditional statistics that the ablated classifier stage would have provided; and a feature set including PTPRC and the naive-T marker program (ideally with exon-4 junction-level quantification). The ranking supports the cell-state hypothesis above, but it cannot ground a molecular mechanism for CD45RA regulation within naive T cells — so my confidence is deliberately moderate-low.
